title: Write RBAC: a Role and a RoleBinding
intro: tutorial-012 had you inspecting RBAC. Now grant the 'ci-bot' ServiceAccount exactly what a deploy pipeline needs in the 'staging' namespace — and nothing more.

steps.prompt: Write a Role named 'deployer' in namespace 'staging' with ONE rule: apiGroups ["apps"], resources ["deployments"], verbs get, list, patch, and update.
steps.hint: Role lives in rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1. 'rules' is a top-level list (not under spec). Deployments are in the 'apps' API group — core resources like pods use the empty group "".
steps.solution:
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: deployer
  namespace: staging
rules:
- apiGroups: ["apps"]
  resources: ["deployments"]
  verbs: ["get", "list", "patch", "update"]
steps.explanation: The permissions exist — but nobody has them yet.
steps.why: No 'delete', no 'create', no secrets, no pods/exec: a deploy pipeline only needs to update an existing Deployment's image. If ci-bot's token ever leaks, the blast radius is 'can change a staging deployment', not 'owns the cluster'.

steps.prompt: Now bind it: a RoleBinding named 'ci-bot-deployer' in namespace 'staging' whose subject is the ServiceAccount 'ci-bot' (namespace staging), referencing the Role 'deployer' (roleRef apiGroup rbac.authorization.k8s.io).
steps.hint: subjects is a list (one binding can grant a role to many identities); roleRef is a single object with kind, name, and apiGroup.
steps.solution:
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: ci-bot-deployer
  namespace: staging
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: ci-bot
  namespace: staging
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: deployer
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
steps.fake_output:
rolebinding.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/ci-bot-deployer created

$ kubectl auth can-i patch deployments -n staging --as=system:serviceaccount:staging:ci-bot
yes
$ kubectl auth can-i delete deployments -n staging --as=system:serviceaccount:staging:ci-bot
no
steps.explanation: ci-bot can now patch deployments in staging, and verifiably can't delete them.
steps.why: Always verify RBAC with 'kubectl auth can-i --as' — both what should be allowed AND what shouldn't. roleRef is immutable after creation: pointing a binding at a different role means deleting and recreating it, a deliberate guard against quietly escalating a binding's permissions.
